title: [Chapitre] II. Réalisations topologiques des réseaux : notes manuscrites (06/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
The page continues the definition, begun on p.1, of a closed subset A of a topological space X being 'régulièrement immergé' (regularly embedded). Let X/A be the quotient that collapses A to a point a. A is regularly embedded if a has a closed neighbourhood V in X/A with a homeomorphism h: V ≅ Cone(B). Here B is compact, h(a) is the cone vertex, and V° = V∖B is open in X/A.

The cone structure gives shrunken copies V_t = tV for 0 ≤ t ≤ 1, each a disjoint union V_t = V_t° ⊔ B_t, where B_t is the level t·B. Because B is compact (tube lemma), the open sets V_t° = tV° form a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of a in X/A.

Let W_t be the inverse image of V_t in X. Every neighbourhood N of A in X gives a neighbourhood of a, since π(int N) is open. Hence the W_t form a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of A in X. Each B_t is closed in X and is the frontier of W_t. Writing W'_t for the exterior X∖W_t, one gets a topological sum decomposition

 X∖B_t = W_t° ⊔ W'_t (interior ⊔ exterior).

So every regularly embedded A has arbitrarily small 'separating collars' whose frontier B_t cuts X into an inside and an outside. In modern terms, W_t∖A ≅ B × (0,t], so A has a mapping-cylinder-type, conelike neighbourhood.

Remarks (NB):
(1) The notion is local. If X' is a neighbourhood of A in X, the condition holds for (A,X) iff it holds for (A,X').
(2) It makes sense for A = ∅: then X/∅ = {a} ⊔ X and B = ∅, the cone on ∅ being a point. The left margin likewise notes that if A is open and closed, a is an isolated point and B = ∅.
(3) It holds for tame ('modéré', e.g. triangulable) subspaces A of a manifold X; the qualifying 'sauf ...' is not finished.

The page then opens a Definition: a 'ficelle topologique' (topological string; 'cellule' is crossed out) is a pair (X,{A,B}) of a space X and an unordered pair of subsets of X. The next page completes it: A and B are closed, non-empty, disjoint and regularly embedded, and the complements are connected after collapsing. This is the topological model of an edge of a 'réseau' or 'vitrail' (a map or graph-like combinatorial structure), with A and B as its two ends. The page serves the goal of building topological realizations of these combinatorial objects inside a 'tame' framework.
errors: Notation slip: W'_t = X − V_t should read X − W_t (or X/A − V_t). Grothendieck identifies X∖A with (X/A)∖{a}.
The letter B is used both for the compact base of the cone and, in the definition at the bottom, for the second end of the ficelle. This is harmless but confusing.

Remark (3) is incomplete: 'convient sauf' breaks off without saying which cases fail. 'Triangulable sub-space of a manifold' alone is not obviously sufficient without local finiteness or compactness hypotheses, given that B is required to be compact.
The statement that the V_t° form a fundamental system of neighbourhoods implicitly uses compactness of B (tube lemma). The hypothesis is stated on p.1, so this is not an error.

ideas.what: A closed subset A ⊂ X is 'regularly embedded' if the collapsed point a in X/A has a closed neighbourhood homeomorphic to the cone on a compact space.
ideas.modern_name: Locally conelike / collared subset; mapping cylinder neighbourhood (cone neighbourhood in X/A)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Siebenmann (locally conelike stratified sets, 1972); M. Brown (collars, 1962); mapping-cylinder neighbourhoods in geometric topology
ideas.where_published: Spirit related to the 'topologie modérée' programme of Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but this definition is not given there.

ideas.what: Consequences: the shrunken neighbourhoods W_t form a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of A, with closed frontier B_t, and X∖B_t is the topological sum of interior and exterior.
Locality of the notion, and the convention A = ∅ with X/∅ = X ⊔ {pt}.
ideas.modern_name: Standard conventions (X/∅ = X_+ in homotopy theory)

ideas.what: 'Ficelle topologique': a space X with an unordered pair of closed, disjoint, regularly embedded 'ends' A, B, as the topological model of an edge of a réseau/vitrail.
ideas.modern_name: Roughly a relative cobordism / 'string' between two ends; topological edge in a realization of a combinatorial map
ideas.usually_credited_to: No exact counterpart; related to realizations of maps and dessins (Jones–Singerman, Shabat–Voevodsky)
ideas.where_published: Possibly connected to the 'réseaux/vitraux' themes of 1985–86 notes; not in published texts to my knowledge.

missed.claim: Grothendieck starts an axiomatic, tame-topology foundation for topological realizations of combinatorial 'réseaux/vitraux', with 'ficelles' as abstract edges defined by intrinsic topological conditions on the ends. This is in place of the usual approach of gluing standard intervals or cells. The criterion for which tame subspaces of manifolds are regularly embedded is left incomplete.
missed.quote: Vraie pour A sous-espace (p. ex triangul.) dans une variété X ... convient sauf
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a concrete instance of the Esquisse 'topologie modérée' programme applied to maps and networks. The mathematics on this page itself, however, is standard collar theory and would not surprise a specialist.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains elementary point-set topology: cone neighbourhoods in X/A, fundamental systems of collars, and conventions. The only distinctive element is the start of the 'ficelle topologique' notion, an intrinsic definition of a topological edge as part of Grothendieck's 1986 réseaux/vitraux realization project. It is interesting historically but not new mathematics on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'paire {A, B} f. Ex(F(A))' is probably 'paire {A,B} ∈ P₂(P(X))' (a 2-element subset of the power set), i.e. an unordered pair of subsets of X.
'Cellule topologique' in the Definition is most likely crossed out or replaced by 'Ficelle topologique', consistent with the heading of p.1 and with conditions 'Fic a)–d)' on p.3.
'W'_t = X − V_t' should be understood as X − W_t (exterior of W_t).
Left margin note: '① A est ouvert et fermé, a est pt isolé, B = ∅ (X/A)', i.e. the degenerate case of an open-closed A.
In ③, the handwriting near 'sous-espace' likely reads 'modéré' (tame) rather than 'variété'.
